<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />confusion with the following {{GHGheb|text=הֵינִקִ֫הוּ}}); {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹלִיךְ}}, but in the 1st sing. of the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} always {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאוֹלֵךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=10}}, &c. Rarely, and almost exclusively late or in poetry, the regular inflexions of {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ}} are also found: ''imperf.'' {{GHGheb|text=יַֽהֲלֹךְ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=9}}, &c.; but {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽהֲלַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=9}}; cf. {{GHGpar|64|a}} and h); {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽהֱלֹךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=22}}, also Mêšaʿ inscription, line 14, {{GHGheb|text=אהלך}}; ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹךְ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=13}} f.16,<ref>Cf. above, m, note 2.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=6|verse=8.9}}); {{GHGterm|imperative plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=הִלְכוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=50}}. On the other hand, the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} is always {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ}}, {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=הֹלֵךְ}}, {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=הָלוֹךְ}}, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽהֱלַךְ}}, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִלֵּךְ}}, {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְהַלֵּךְ}}, so that a {{GHGheb|text=י}} never appears unmistakably as the first radical. The usual explanation of the above forms is nevertheless based on a supposed obsolete {{GHGheb|text=יָלַךְ}}. It is, however, more correct to regard the apparent {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} forms of {{GHGheb|text=הלך}} with Praetorius ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} ii. 310 ff.) as originating with the Hiphʿîl, of which the ground-form ''hahlîkh'' became ''hâlîkh'', and this again, on the analogy of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}}, ''hôlîkh''. This ''hôlîkh'' being referred to a supposed ''haulîkh'' (properly ''hawlîkh'') gave rise to new formations after the manner of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}.<section end=par69 />
<section begin=par70 />{{GHGpar-heading|70|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}. Second Class, or Verbs properly {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=יָטַב}} to be good. Paradigm L}}

<div style="font-size: small; text-align: center;">Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 143 ff.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 603 ff.</div>

Verbs properly {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} differ from verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} in the following points:

{{GHGmargin-letter|70|a}}
'''1.''' In {{GHGterm|Qal}} the initial Yôdh never suffers aphaeresis or elision; hence the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} has the form {{GHGheb|text=יְבֹשׁ}},<ref>This may be inferred from {{GHGheb|text=בִּיבֹשׁ}} (={{GHGheb|text=בִּיְ׳}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=11}}, which with its fem. {{GHGheb|text=יְבֹ֫שֶׁת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}}, is the only example of an infinitive ''construct Qal'' of these verbs. No example of the {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} is found: consequently the forms {{GHGheb|text=יְטַב}}, &c. (in Paradigm L of the earlier editions of this Grammar), are only inferred from the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.</ref> the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִיטַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִיקַץ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִינַק}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִינָק}}), also written {{GHGheb|text=יִטַב}}, &c.; and so always with a tone-bearing ''ă'' in the second syllable, even after {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּיקַ֫ץ}}, except {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫יקֶץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=24}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫יצֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=7.19}}, unless {{GHGheb|text=יָצַר}} is to be included among verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נוֹצַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=10}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|70|b}}
'''2.''' In {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the original form {{GHGheb|text=הַיְטִיב}} is regularly contracted to {{GHGheb|text=הֵיטִיב}} (rarely written {{GHGheb|text=הֵטִיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵיטִב}}, &c.); {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵיטִיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫יטֶב}}. Instances of the uncontracted form are {{GHGheb|text=יַיְשִׁ֫רוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=25}}, according to Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|67|p}}), an example of an ''i-imperfect'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, since the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} is otherwise always ''causative''; {{GHGheb|text=הַיְשַׁר}} ({{GHGterm|imperative}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=9}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} requires {{GHGheb|text=הושׁר}} according to the form of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=אושׁר}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲיַשֵּׁר}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=17}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַיְמִינִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=2}}, to be explained as a denominative from {{GHGheb|text=יָמִין}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַיְסִירֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=12}} ({{GHGpar|24|f}}, note), but perhaps the punctuation here is only intended to suggest another reading {{GHGheb|text=אֲיַסְּרֵם}}.
